sanskrit_verse:
गर्भाधानं ऋतौ पुंसः सवनं स्पन्दनात् पुरा ।
षष्ठेऽष्टमे वा सीमन्तो मास्येते जातकर्म च ॥१.११॥
transliteration: garbhādhānaṃ ṛtau puṃsaḥ savanaṃ spandanāt purā | ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā sīmanto māsy ete jātakarma ca ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Conception occurs in the fertile season of a man; the ritual of impregnation precedes gestational movement. The Sīmantonnayana rite is performed in the sixth or eighth month, followed by Jātakarma upon birth.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of biological rhythm as determinant of lawful action
Causation through sequential ritual alignment with cosmic order
Capacity-based responsibility rooted in physiological readiness
Restoration logic via timely sacramental observance
Consciousness alignment through prenatal and perinatal samskāras
executable_legal_axioms: IF gestational duration reaches sixth OR eighth lunar month THEN execute Sīmantonnayana without exception
IF fetal movement detected AND paternal lineage confirmed THEN initiate garbhādhāna completion protocol
IF birth event occurs THEN execute Jātakarma within twelve nadikas ELSE invoke temporal misalignment correction
IF seasonal fertility cycle aligns with procreative intent THEN permit lawful conception ELSE defer until alignment restored
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning parental rights, reproductive autonomy, and neonatal welfare, the Court shall recognize ritually timed gestational rites as prima facie evidence of lawful intentionality and conscious alignment with Sanātana Dharma’s bio-temporal jurisprudence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causality through observed fetal motion and seasonal congruence. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential sacraments restoring familial dharma. Responsibility is proportional to awareness of ritually correct timing. No punitive consequence arises from omission; only completion process applies.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Delayed sīmantonnayana must be executed immediately upon recognition
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Parents affirm conscious participation in delayed rites
Capacity Restoration: Instructional guidance provided to ensure future compliance with timing
Integrity Reintegration: Community affirmation reaffirms child's dharmic entry into family lineage
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this verse is established as source-law governing procreative rhythm, gestational ritual, and neonatal integration. Dharma is restored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness remains the supreme adjudicator.
